capability.summary: Run the Rust project's default `cargo test` command from a supplied project path
capability.description: Validates one path, chooses it as the working directory when it is a directory or uses its parent when it is a file, then executes `cargo test` with no additional arguments. The wrapper returns captured Cargo output and treats only exit code 0 as success.
capability.problem_space: Default Rust test-suite execution through Cargo for one local project path; not language-agnostic testing, test discovery without execution, coverage reporting, or arbitrary Cargo command execution.

env_requirements: cargo executable and a compatible Rust toolchain
constraint.io_signature: Input: one required existing Rust project directory or a path inside its root; output: a JSON process envelope with Cargo's exit code and full stdout/stderr.
accepted_inputs: an existing Rust project directory containing the Cargo project to test
an existing file path whose parent directory is the Cargo project working directory
constraint.output_shape: Passing run: {status: "success", tool: "cargo", target: string, exit_code: 0, result: null, stdout: string, stderr: string|null}, then process exit 0. Failed tests, compilation failures, or other nonzero Cargo results use the same keys with status="tool_error" and propagate Cargo's exit code. Missing path/executable/300-second timeout: {status: "error", tool: "cargo", message: string}, exiting 2/3/4. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: always runs the default `cargo test` with no package, workspace, feature, target, filter, release, or passthrough test arguments
uses a fixed 300-second timeout and captures stdout/stderr without parsing or truncation
Cargo may compile code, create or update build artifacts such as `target/`, resolve dependencies, and otherwise produce normal Cargo project side effects
a supplied file is not tested individually; only its parent directory is used as the Cargo working directory

output_contract.description: JSON process envelope containing the default `cargo test` status, actual exit code, target, and full captured stdout/stderr.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run the default Rust test suite with cargo test
execute Cargo tests for a local Rust project
negative_intents: run Python, JavaScript, Go, or language-agnostic tests
generate Rust test coverage or parse structured test results
run arbitrary Cargo subcommands or pass custom cargo test flags
